rubrics.rubric: Does the ABC-Supplier Matrix correctly identify E & J Gallo Winery as the dominant supplier in A-class revenue (approximately 42-43% of total warehouse sales, with ~205 A-class items), and Republic National as having the most total SKUs (~814) but disproportionately concentrated in C-class items (~570 C-class items)?
criterion: The cross-tabulation must show each supplier's SKU counts and revenue share across A/B/C tiers
E & J Gallo Winery must be identified as dominant with ~42.7% of total warehouse sales revenue and the highest count of A-class items (~205)
Republic National Distributing Co must be shown as having the most total SKUs (~814) but ranking only 3rd in revenue (~14.5%), with an extremely long tail of C-class items (~570)

Southern Glazers (4th in SKU count at ~493 but meaningful A-class revenue) and The Country Vintner/Winebow (~794 SKUs but only ~12.7% of revenue, heavily skewed toward C-class at ~536 items) must also be characterized

rubrics.rubric: Does the analysis correctly identify dead stock items by supplier and flag that The Country Vintner/Winebow and Republic National have disproportionately high dead stock concentrations, including specific high-value items like Valdespino Pedro Ximenez ($29.00 unit cost, 31 units on hand, $0 annual COGS), La Spinetta Vermentino ($28.19 unit cost, 22 units on hand, $0 COGS), and Cardinale Napa Cab ($64.37 unit cost, 17 units on hand, $0 COGS)?
criterion: Dead stock must be defined as items with zero warehouse sales in the last 6 months of available data, identified via $0.00 Annual COGS 2020 while carrying significant on-hand inventory

Notable dead stock examples from Winebow must be identified, including Delaille Unique S/Blc (50 units, $20.14 each), Eugene Carrel Cremant de Savoie (58 units, $6.58 each), Valdespino Pedro Ximenez (31 units, $29.00 each), and La Spinetta Vermentino (22 units, $28.19 each)

Notable dead stock examples from Republic National must be identified, including Cardinale Napa Cab (17 units, $64.37 each), Klinker Brick Rose (45 units, $21.24 each), and Seacrets Vodka (57 units, $25.17 each)
The analysis must connect dead stock to tied-up working capital and warehouse space consumption

rubrics.rubric: Does the Demand Volatility & Reorder Analysis correctly calculate the coefficient of variation (CV) of monthly warehouse sales for A-class items and identify items with high demand variability (CV > 1.0), such as Barossa Valley Estate GSM (CV ~1.56), Sunseeker Rose (CV ~1.53), and Lagunitas Sumpin Sumpin 4/6 NR (CV ~1.41)?
criterion: The CV calculation must use standard deviation divided by mean of monthly warehouse sales across available data periods

Most A-class items should show CV < 0.5 (relatively stable demand), with approximately 15 items having CV > 1.0 (highly volatile), including Barossa Valley Estate GSM (~1.56), Sunseeker Rose (~1.53), and Lagunitas Sumpin Sumpin 4/6 NR (~1.41)
The analysis must note data sparsity limitations: items appear in only a subset of 15 available months, and 2020 only has 4 months of data (Jan, Mar, Jul, Sep)
Items with CV = 0 due to appearing in only one period should not be misrepresented as having stable demand

rubrics.rubric: Does the Supplier Scorecard use the correct weighting formula — on-time delivery rate (30%), order accuracy (25%), average lead time vs. contract terms (20%), quality issue rate (15%), and year-over-year spend trend (10%) — and correctly rank E & J Gallo Winery as the top performer and Legends Ltd as the worst performer?
criterion: The composite score must use exactly these weights: OTD 30%, accuracy 25%, lead time 20%, quality 15%, YoY spend 10%
E & J Gallo must rank #1 (95.0% OTD, 98.74% accuracy, 3.3-day avg lead time) and Southern Glazers must rank #2 (90.63% OTD, 93.74% accuracy, 4.0-day lead time)

Republic National must rank middle (73.33% OTD, 92.74% accuracy, 5.4-day lead time), Winebow #4 (77.27% OTD, 99.35% accuracy, 7.3-day lead time), and Legends Ltd last (56.25% OTD, 13.37-day avg lead time)
Since only 2020 data exists, the YoY spend trend component should be noted as limited or estimated

rubrics.rubric: Does the scorecard provide a data-supported renewal recommendation for The Country Vintner/Winebow that accounts for their 77.27% on-time delivery rate, 7.31-day average lead time, disproportionate dead stock contribution, and their contract expiring February 28, 2021?
criterion: The Supplier Scorecard's renewal recommendation must address Winebow's below-average on-time delivery at 77.27% (below 80% average) and 7.31-day average lead time (2nd longest)

The Supplier Scorecard's renewal recommendation must highlight Winebow's lowest spend ($182,428, 13.8% of total) despite 794 SKUs (2nd most), indicating very low average revenue per SKU, plus extensive dead stock (e.g., Delaille Unique S/Blc 50 units at $20.14, Valdespino Pedro Ximenez 31 units at $29.00)
Two months with zero orders (Feb and Jun 2020) and the contract expiration of February 28, 2021 (59 days from data end) must be noted in the Supplier Scorecard's renewal recommendation

The Supplier Scorecard's renewal recommendation should consider whether the catalog breadth justifies the poor velocity, and if termination is recommended, estimate the SKU migration scope (~794 SKUs)

rubrics.rubric: Does the revised SOP substitute static reorder points with dynamic reorder points calculated using average monthly demand and actual supplier lead times, referencing specific supplier lead times (E & J Gallo: ~3.3 days, Southern Glazers: ~4.0 days, Republic National: ~5.4 days, Winebow: ~7.3 days, Legends Ltd: ~13.4 days)?
criterion: The revised SOP must replace the annual static reorder point methodology (Inefficiency #2) with a dynamic calculation that incorporates actual supplier lead times from the database
The new methodology must use demand-driven calculations (e.g., average daily demand × lead time + safety stock) and account for seasonal demand variation
Specific lead time differences between suppliers must be referenced, particularly Legends Ltd's 13.4-day average (requiring higher reorder points) vs. E & J Gallo's 3.3-day average
The formula or methodology must be clearly documented in the SOP with sufficient detail for warehouse staff to apply it

rubrics.rubric: Does the revised SOP retain the original document's section structure (Purpose & Scope, Current Process Overview, Process Steps 1-9, Known Issues, Roles & Responsibilities) and present changes as tracked revisions or clearly marked redline annotations rather than as an entirely new document?
criterion: The revised SOP must retain the original SOP-WH-2024-003's section structure with its 6 top-level sections and 9 process steps

Changes must be presented as tracked revisions (e.g., strikethrough for deletions, highlighted/colored text for additions) or clearly marked redline annotations (e.g., '[REVISED]', '[ADDED]', '[DELETED]' markers)
The document must NOT be a complete rewrite — the original procedural framework should be visible with modifications layered on top, allowing reviewers to see exactly what changed

rubrics.rubric: Does the Excel workbook demonstrate proper interlinking between the three sheets (ABC-Supplier Matrix, Demand Volatility & Reorder Analysis, and Supplier Scorecard), such that the ABC classification feeds into both the reorder analysis and the supplier scorecard evaluation?
criterion: The ABC classification from Sheet 1 must be used in Sheet 2 to focus the reorder analysis on A-class items

Dead stock identification from Sheet 1 must be referenced in Sheet 3's supplier evaluation, and reorder misalignment findings from Sheet 2 must inform Sheet 3's supplier scorecard (e.g., suppliers with more misaligned items score lower)
Average inventory turns per ABC-supplier cell in Sheet 1 should connect to the overall inventory performance discussion within the workbook
The workbook must show integration across all three sheets as an integrated analysis, not three siloed reports, as the VP explicitly requested
